answer: Proof of space curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit dedicated storage sectors. Verifiers challenge cryptographic tables unfolding like a lotus to confirm continuous data retention. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning physical disks per identity, denying botnets a haven. Because raw plots cannot shrink to the size of a walnut, cloning demands tangible hardware. However, adversaries with surplus enterprise storage can still amass identities at low marginal cost.
